cues.en: Training RNN's, just like CNN's, it's hard, and in some ways it's even harder.
cues.zh: 訓練 RNN，和 CNN 一樣困難，某些方面甚至更難。

cues.en: The main twist here is that we need to back-propagate not only through the neural network itself and all of its layers, but also through time.
cues.zh: 主要差異是，不只要反向傳播經過神經網路與所有層，也要沿著時間反向傳播。

cues.en: From a practical standpoint, every one of those time steps ends up looking like another layer in our neural network while we're trying to train it, and those times steps can add up fast.
cues.zh: 實務上，訓練時，每個時間步都像神經網路另一層，而時間步會快速累積。

cues.en: Over time we can end up with a deeper and deeper neural network that we need to train, and the cost of actually performing gradient descent on that increasingly deep neural network becomes increasingly large.
cues.zh: 隨時間，待訓練網路越來越深，對不斷加深的網路做梯度下降，成本也越來越高。

cues.en: So to put an upper cap on that training time, often we limit the backpropagation to a limited number of time steps.
cues.zh: 因此，為訓練時間設上限，通常只對有限時間步反向傳播。

cues.en: We call this, truncated backpropagation through time.
cues.zh: 這稱為截斷式隨時間反向傳播。

cues.en: It's something to keep in mind when you're training an RNN.
cues.zh: 訓練 RNN 時，必須記得。

cues.en: You not only need to backpropagate through the neural network topology that you've created, you also need to backpropagate through all of the time steps that you've built up to that point.
cues.zh: 不只要通過建立的神經網路拓樸反向傳播，也要通過累積到當下的所有時間步。

cues.en: Now, we talked earlier about the fact that as you're building up an RNN, the state from earlier time steps end up getting diluted over time because we just keep feeding in behavior
cues.zh: 前面說過，建立 RNN 時，早期時間步的狀態，會隨時間稀釋，因為不斷把前一步的行為，

cues.en: from the previous step in our run to the current step.
cues.zh: 送入目前這一步。

cues.en: This can be a problem if you have a system where older behavior does not matter less than newer behavior.
cues.zh: 如果系統中，舊行為並不比新行為次要，這可能是問題。

cues.en: For example, if you're looking at words in a sentence, the words at the beginning of a sentence might be even more important than the words toward the end.
cues.zh: 例如，查看句子中的詞時，句首的詞，甚至可能比句尾更重要。

cues.en: If you're trying to learn the meaning of a sentence, there is no inherent relationship between where each word is and how important it might be in many cases.
cues.zh: 學習句意時，很多情況，詞的位置與重要性，沒有內在關係。

cues.en: That's an example of where you might want to do something to counteract that effect.
cues.zh: 這就是可能需要對抗這個效果的例子。

cues.en: One way to do that is something called the LSTM cell.
cues.zh: 一種方式，叫做 LSTM 單元。

cues.en: It stands for Long Short-Term Memory cell.
cues.zh: 代表長短期記憶單元。

cues.en: The idea here is that it maintains separate ideas of both short-term and long-term states, and it does this in a fairly complex way.
cues.zh: 概念是，分別維持短期與長期狀態，實作方式相當複雜。

cues.en: Now, fortunately for you, you don't really need to understand the nitty-gritty details of how it works.
cues.zh: 幸好，不必理解所有細節。

cues.en: There is an image of it here for you to look at if you're curious, but the libraries that you use will implement this for you.
cues.zh: 有興趣可以看這張圖，但使用的函式庫會替你實作。

cues.en: The important thing to understand is that if you're dealing with a sequence of data where you don't want to give preferential treatment to more recent data, you probably want to use an LSTM cell
cues.zh: 重要的是，如果資料序列中，不希望優先重視近期資料，大概應該使用 LSTM 單元，

cues.en: instead of just using a straight-up RNN.
cues.zh: 而不是單純 RNN。

cues.en: There's also an optimization on top of LSTM cells called GRU cells, G-R-U cells.
cues.zh: LSTM 還有一種最佳化，叫做 GRU 單元，G-R-U。

cues.en: That stands for Gated Recurrent Unit.
cues.zh: 代表閘控循環單元。

cues.en: It's just a simplification on LSTM cells that performs almost as well, so if you need to strike a compromise between performance in terms of how well your model works, and performance in terms
cues.zh: 它是 LSTM 的簡化版，表現幾乎一樣好，因此若要在模型表現，與

cues.en: of how long it takes to train it, a GRU cell might be a good choice.
cues.zh: 訓練所需時間之間取捨，GRU 可能是不錯的選擇。

cues.en: GRU cells are very popular in practice, and later we'll see how they can be used for certain types of recommender systems as well.
cues.zh: GRU 實務上很熱門，稍後也會看到，如何用在某些推薦系統。

cues.en: Training a RNN is really hard.
cues.zh: 訓練 RNN 真的很難。

cues.en: If you thought CNN's were hard, wait till you see RNN's.
cues.zh: 如果覺得 CNN 難，等看到 RNN 就知道。

cues.en: They are very sensitive to the topologies you choose and the choice of hyperparameters.
cues.zh: 它對拓樸與超參數的選擇，非常敏感。

cues.en: And since we have to simulate things over time and not just through the static topology of your network, they can become extremely resource intensive.
cues.zh: 因為要沿時間模擬，不只通過靜態網路拓樸，可能極為耗費資源。

cues.en: If you make the wrong choices, you might have a recurrent neural network that doesn't converge at all.
cues.zh: 選錯時，循環神經網路可能完全不收斂。

cues.en: It might be completely useless even after you've run it for hours to see if it actually works.
cues.zh: 即使跑了數小時，想確認能不能運作，最後仍可能毫無用處。

cues.en: So again, it's important to build upon previous research when you can.
cues.zh: 因此，再次強調，能利用既有研究時，就要利用。

cues.en: Try to find some sets of topologies and parameters that work well for similar problems to what you're trying to do.
cues.zh: 試著找出對相似問題有效的拓樸與參數組合。
